findings.note: N.D.C.C. 12-60.1-03: the participant serves the prosecuting attorney and files a petition, a mandatory proposed order and a proof of service with the clerk of the existing criminal case. Nothing happens unless the participant files. This is the property the rejected 12-60.1-05 route lacks.

The petition asks for sealing of court and prosecution records and for the findings 12-60.1-04(1) requires. It does not ask any agency outside the court and prosecution to act. The default agency-wide relief is asserted absent by test, and the order states what it does not reach.

Chapter 12-60.1 with the operative sections. The ground-specific citation is 12-60.1-02(1)(a) for the misdemeanor ground, matching the committed registry excerpt's legal name. No subsection is attributed beyond what the committed sources carry.

Three grounds, exactly the three 12-60.1-02 states. The pardon ground carries no clean period and the packet does not allege one for it. The 12-60.1-04(1)(c) and (d) findings are required on every ground, including the pardon ground, because a pardon is not a substitute for them.

Three bars, carried verbatim from the state pack, each denying the route on every ground. The impaired-driving bar routes to 39-08-01.6 rather than merely refusing. The statutory basis of the impaired-driving bar is recorded as a source silence, because 12-60.1-02(2) as read at source does not state it.

Every content item ndFilingInstructions[4] requires is alleged. Fidelity to ndRequiredFields is enforced at module load, so a state-pack revision that adds a field breaks the build rather than shipping a petition that no longer collects it.

No fee amount is stated anywhere, and a test asserts no dollar figure appears. No committed source establishes one. The participant is told to ask the clerk both for the fee and about proceeding without payment of fees. Recorded as a source silence and a release blocker.

Five stop conditions, each traced to a committed rule and each stating what the participant does. The 45-day floor, the clear-and-convincing burden and the up-to-one-year refiling bar are stated before filing.
A plain declaration with no penalty recital. No committed source ties a verification statute to this petition; the silence is carried as a counsel flag rather than filled with a general oath statute.
No sentence in the output asserts a rule not traceable to the ND state pack, the compiled ND engine profile, or the committed Chapter 12-60.1 pleading registry excerpts.
Sealing-first throughout. runPleadingQa blocks expungement, expunge, set aside, annulment and vacatur in the rendered pleading and passes.
Seven other-state sovereigns, courts and agencies asserted absent; three required North Dakota terms asserted present.
